hero.intro.catalogSourceText: Heart racing before a presentation? Navy SEALs use this technique before high-stakes missions. 4-6 cycles (about 90 seconds) will calm your nerves so you can speak clearly and confidently.

prose.title.catalogSourceText: Why box breathing works for presentation anxiety

prose.paragraphs.0.text.catalogSourceText: When you're about to present, your brain can't distinguish between a boardroom and a life-threatening situation. It triggers the same ancient alarm system: adrenaline floods your bloodstream, your heart races, blood diverts from your brain to your muscles. This was useful for outrunning predators, not so helpful for explaining Q3 results.

prose.paragraphs.1.after.catalogSourceText: through two mechanisms. First, the structured 4-4-4-4 counting occupies your prefrontal cortex (thinking brain), preventing it from spinning worst-case scenarios. Second, the slow, even rhythm activates your parasympathetic nervous system, the “rest and digest” mode that tells your body the threat has passed.

prose.paragraphs.2.text.catalogSourceText: Mark Divine, a retired Navy SEAL Commander, introduced box breathing to BUD/S training because SEALs needed a technique that worked reliably under extreme pressure. If it helps operators stay calm during combat, it can help you nail your next presentation.

numberedSteps.steps.0.title.catalogSourceText: Find a quiet spot (5-10 minutes before)

numberedSteps.steps.0.body.catalogSourceText: Bathroom stall, hallway, your car, or any private space.

numberedSteps.steps.1.body.catalogSourceText: Drop your shoulders, unclench your jaw, relax your hands.

numberedSteps.steps.2.title.catalogSourceText: Inhale through your nose for 4 counts

numberedSteps.steps.2.body.catalogSourceText: Let your belly expand. Keep it quiet and controlled.

numberedSteps.steps.3.body.catalogSourceText: Stay relaxed. This shouldn't feel strained.

numberedSteps.steps.4.body.catalogSourceText: Through your nose or pursed lips. Let tension leave with the breath.

numberedSteps.steps.5.title.catalogSourceText: Hold empty for 4 counts, then repeat

numberedSteps.steps.5.body.catalogSourceText: Complete 4-6 cycles total. You should feel noticeably calmer.

faq.items.0.question.catalogSourceText: How long before a presentation should I do box breathing?

faq.items.0.answer.catalogSourceText: Start 5-10 minutes before your presentation for best results. Do 4-6 cycles (about 90 seconds) in a quiet spot. If you feel nerves rising while waiting, do another quick set of 2-3 cycles. The effects last 15-30 minutes.

faq.items.1.question.catalogSourceText: Why do Navy SEALs use box breathing?

faq.items.1.answer.catalogSourceText: Navy SEALs use box breathing because it reliably activates the parasympathetic nervous system within 60-90 seconds. The structured 4-count rhythm gives the mind something to focus on while the slow pace physiologically lowers heart rate and cortisol, exactly what you need before high-stakes situations.

faq.items.2.question.catalogSourceText: Can I do box breathing right before I speak?

faq.items.2.answer.catalogSourceText: Yes! If you're being introduced or waiting to take the stage, do 2-3 silent cycles. Breathe through your nose, count in your head, and keep your shoulders relaxed. No one will notice, and you'll feel noticeably calmer when you start speaking.
